newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Dini urges greater autonomy for Kosovo.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini urges greater autonomy for Kosovo.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini called on Belgrade on Monday to grant more autonomy to the troubled Serbian province of Kosovo, where the majority of residents are ethnic Albanians, the foreign ministry said.

"The Minister underlined that Italy...encourages the Belgrade government to enable progress in granting greater autonomy, in particular in the education sector, on the basis of a deal underwritten last September," it said in a statement.
The statement was issued after Dini held talks with Ibrahim Rugova, visiting leader of the Democratic League of Kosovo (LDK), the biggest ethnic Albanian party in the province.

The landmark deal on education was brokered by an Italian Roman Catholic peace group, the Sant'Egidio Community and allowed for Albanian students to return to Serbia's mainstream education system after a six-year boycott.

"Minister Dini underlined the need, shared by the international community, to favour...the relaunch of dialogue between the parties with the aim of ensuring full autonomy in the region in a gradual, peaceful way and with respect to the existing borders," it said in a statement.

The LDK advocates peaceful resistance to Serb rule and Rugova and other leaders of almost two million Albanians have been pushing for their own Kosovo republic within the new Yugoslavia comprising Serbia and Montenegro.

Albanians, who outnumber Serbs nine to one in the province, have boycotted Serbian institutions since 1989 when Serbia's President Slobodan Milosevic cracked down on Kosovo, saying Albanians wanted to secede.
Serbs consider Kosovo the cradle of their civilisation.

Dini told Rugova that Italy was committed to the process of national reconciliation in Albania, adding that a return to normality in the troubled neighbouring state could only have positive effects on Kosovo and the Balkans in general.
Italy has led a multinational security force to Albania to oversee aid distribution and elections on June 29 and July 6. It has said it plans to withdraw the force by August 12.
